# `get_focuser_value`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read one focuser control value by name.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build established) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd3480, myStristr @0x6dc530 (64-bit build) |

Requires an open focuser. Of the three named controls only max_step (the cached UI maximum, an integer) yields an ordinary success. In the 64-bit build a recognised backlash on an open handle always fails (the driver read is a stub), logging and replying 300; the 32-bit backend is a separate implementation whose outcome is unresolved. reset_step has no getter (210). The handler can encode integer, float, boolean and string values internally; an unexpected value tag gives 300. The strict grade is MUTATOR because both builds write diagnostic log state on the failure path; no device setting is changed.

Side effects: Reads cached state; the backlash failure path writes diagnostic log state. No open, move or close.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_focuser_value"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | yes | - | A control name as a scalar string, or an array whose first element is the name. Absent, empty, null or non-string gives 105. Matching is a case-insensitive substring search of the given string within each canonical name (max_step, backlash, reset_step); the first match wins and an empty string matches nothing (109). [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | params absent, empty, null or name not a string | `expected string param` |
| 109 | Name matches none of max_step, backlash, reset_step (including the empty string) | `unexpected param` |
| 318 | Recognised control but the focuser is not open | `device not connected` |
| 210 | Recognised control with no getter (reset_step) | `not supported` |
| 300 | Backlash read fails (always, in the 64-bit build) or the value has an unexpected type | `internal error` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":14,"method":"get_focuser_value","params":["max_step"]}
```

Request, scalar-name - Scalar name form:

```json
{"id":15,"method":"get_focuser_value","params":"max_step"}
```

Reply, ok - max_step (value invented):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_focuser_value","result":2600,"code":0,"id":14}
```

Reply, backlash-fails - Backlash read on an open focuser (64-bit build):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_focuser_value","error":"internal error","code":300,"id":16}
```
